value.name: HBO promo airs about Lowell documentary
value.description: A TV plays a promo for the upcoming HBO documentary about Lowell and "High on Crack Street."
evidence: CRACK STREET' PLAYS ON A TV LOWELL MAN ON THE STREET DOCUMENTARY INTERVIEWS. REAL INTERVIEWS WITH REAL LOWELL. TALKING ABOUT "HIGH ON CRACK STREET" AIRING THAT NIGHT...

value.name: Lowell residents criticize the film
value.description: The promo shows locals saying the documentary makes Lowell look bad and blames Micky and Dicky for hurting the city.
evidence: HEARD IT MAKES THE CITY LOOK BAD...MICKY & DICKY BAD FOR THE CITY... DREAM IS DEAD...

value.name: Micky enters Dunkin' Donuts
value.description: Micky rushes into a crowded Dunkin' Donuts in the rain, looking tired and out of shape with his healed hand still bothering him.
evidence: DUNKIN' DONUTS - CHELMSFORD ST., LOWELL - DAY Raining. Micky runs into a crowded Dunkin' Donuts, tired, dark circles, out-of-shape. HAND HEALED, HABITUALLY STRETCHING AND CLENCHING IT.

value.name: Customers stare at Micky
value.description: The people in the shop notice Micky immediately and begin whispering about him.
evidence: Everybody looking at him, some whisper.

value.name: Micky greets Mickey O'Keefe
value.description: Micky spots Mickey O'Keefe in the back of the shop and calls out to him.
evidence: Micky's eyes wide, catches sight of Mickey O'Keefe in the back drinking coffee, reading the newspaper, still in his police uniform.

value.name: Mickey O'Keefe hugs and checks Micky's hand
value.description: Mickey O'Keefe stands up, hugs Micky, and asks how his hand is healing.
evidence: MICKEY O'KEEFE (stands, hugs Micky hello) How's ya hand?!

value.name: Mickey invites Micky to the gym
value.description: Mickey O'Keefe jokes with Micky and tells him to come down to the gym if he wants.
evidence: Why don't ya come down to the gym if ya want? Ya fat fuck, look atcha.

value.name: Micky worries about HBO movie attention
value.description: Micky complains that the HBO movie will make everyone stare at him as if he did something wrong.
evidence: Now I gotta worry about this movie tonight on HBO, everybody lookin' at me like I did somethin' wrong, ain't my fault he's on TV.

value.name: Mickey advises Micky to avoid the movie
value.description: Mickey O'Keefe tells Micky it is better if he does not watch the film because it will only make him feel bad.
evidence: It's bettah for ya if ya don't see it, Micky, it's just gonna make ya feel bad.

value.name: Mickey defends Micky to the crowd
value.description: Mickey O'Keefe turns on the staring customers and tells them Micky will not be on TV because it is his crazy brother.
evidence: [turns to everyone] What are you lookin' at? He ain't gonna be on TV, it's his crazy brothah.

value.name: Crowd continues staring
value.description: The people in the shop keep staring at Micky and Mickey despite the confrontation.
